newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian official denies tie to Sibneft buyer.
newsitem.headline: Russian official denies tie to Sibneft buyer.

text.p: Boris Berezovsky, the business magnate who holds a senior Kremlin security post, denied on Tuesday that he had any links to the mystery buyer of a majority stake in Russia's seventh biggest oil producer, Sibneft.

"I have no ties to FNK," Berezovsky told Reuters when asked if OOO Finansovaya Neftyanaya Korporatsiya (FNK), which acquired 51 percent of Sibneft at an auction on Monday, was linked to ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK), which organised the tender and is part of Berezovsky's diversified business empire.

Berezovsky stressed he had suspended his active involvement in business on being named deputy secretary of the Kremlin Security Council last autumn. He played a leading role in negotiating the peace treaty President Boris Yeltsin signed on Monday with the leader of Russia's breakaway Chechnya region.

Russian media and financial analysts have speculated that, as in a number of similar tenders for former state companies, the winning bid for Sibneft was awarded to a company closely related to the group organising the auction and that Berezovsky, through NFK and FNK, now had control of Sibneft.
Sibneft, which has a controlling stake in oil producer Noyabrskneftegaz NYGS.RTS, said the identity of the owners of the previously unknown FNK would probably be revealed next week.
